correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 21–83. Expanding (x²+√2xy−y²)² cancels the mixed quadratic term and gives 2+2√2(P−Q) on integration. If δ is the L2 norm of this defect and e1,e2,e3 are its pairings with x²,y²,xy, then e1−e2−√2e3=2−4E and e1+e2=√2(P+Q); Hölder gives |ei|≤δ. The displayed P,Q,E estimates give |3E−P²−Q²−5/4|≤7δ≤12√d using |P²−P0²|≤(1+1/(2√2))|P−P0| and similarly for Q. Differentiating the square root of the norm fourth power gives the third-derivative bound 72/||z||4 for unit directions; along either segment ||z||4≥7/8, so the Taylor remainder bound 24h³ is conservative. The corresponding norm second derivative is nonnegative and ≤3/||z||4, validating the ≤8 bound used for the difference of the two norms. The arithmetic mean squared subtracts (u−v)²/4 from the quadratic-mean square, costing at most 2√2h²d+32h⁴. The remaining coefficient of hd is ≥1/2; completing the square costs 72h³, and 32h⁴≤4h³, giving 100. Two disjoint supported unit functions exist in any real L4 of dimension at least two: the finite measure weighted by |x|⁴+|y|⁴ for independent x,y must admit a positive split, or their normalized coordinate functions are constant on its only atom. The given a,b pair has E=1/2 and P=−Q=−1/(2√2); its two outputs are coordinate permutations with signs and thus have equal norm. This gives the common upper bound, including the maximum endpoint, and the square root has coefficient 9/16. The frozen finite verifier was inspected, not executed; the analytic proof, not the finite checks, establishes the bound.

value.rationale: A sharp curvature coefficient uniform through the maximum-mean endpoint is a worthwhile result, but is established in the matching indexed theorem, which also gives near-minimizer rigidity. The only nominal increment, the deliberately conservative constant 100 at the same local cutoff, is neither mathematically motivated nor stronger than an explicit reckoning of the existing estimates.
